deep_dive.title: Escaping cells dilute CRISPR screen responses unequally across cell types
deep_dive.abstract: Single-cell CRISPR screens run in many cell types are used to compare how cell types respond to perturbation, to train models that transfer effects between them and to score such models. These uses assume that cells carrying a guide RNA had their target knocked down. Yet cells grow for days before sequencing: when an essential gene is knocked down, knocked-down cells are depleted or stop dividing while cells that escaped knockdown keep growing, and the measured response, an average over all cells carrying the guide, is diluted. We define the escape fraction of a perturbation as the share of its measured cells whose target was not effectively knocked down, and estimate it from each cell's counts of the targeted gene with a two-group mixture that recovers known fractions in simulated mixtures. In most cell types the escape fraction rises with how essential the gene is, it is higher in a later screen of the same cells, and it reaches about half of the measured cells in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). It predicts how much each response is diluted: the response size falls to (1 - e)^2 of that of the knocked-down cells. Because the escape fraction differs between cell types, it changes all three uses: hESCs respond like K562 cells unless knockdown depletes them, the coefficient a simple transfer model learns is lowered by the dilution of the cell type it predicts, and a benchmark scored on all cells rewards predictions shrunk towards no change, partly because that ground truth is itself diluted. Where cells stop dividing instead, the response also contains expression differences between cell-cycle stages. Response sizes should be compared on knocked-down cells or corrected for the escape fraction.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Defines the escape fraction of a CRISPR perturbation as the share of cells not effectively knocked down, estimates it per cell from targeted-gene counts via a two-group mixture, and shows this dilution of measured response differs across cell types, biasing comparisons and response models.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 在多细胞类型的单细胞CRISPR筛选中，携带guide RNA的细胞常因逃逸敲低而使测得的扰动响应被稀释，影响细胞类型间比较与扰动响应预测模型的训练评分。作者将逃逸比例定义为未有效敲低细胞所占份额，并利用靶基因计数以两组混合模型从单细胞层面估计该比例。分析显示逃逸造成的稀释在不同细胞类型间并不均等，从而系统性地扭曲扰动效应比较。该工作为校正CRISPR筛选响应、提升扰动响应预测可靠性提供了可操作的度量与校正思路。

quick_skim.title: An autoencoder outperforms two transformers on prediction of gene expression from chromatin accessibility
quick_skim.abstract: Models that predict RNA abundance from chromatin accessibility are rarely compared under the same features, targets and metrics. We built one benchmark on 126,604 paired single-nucleus profiles from 19 human studies with a shared vocabulary of 50,000 peaks and 3,185 genes, ten 5x2 cross-validation folds and one scoring target, and compared seven implemented pipelines and two reference predictors across 70 trained runs; each pipeline keeps its own input normalisation and native training target. The scButterfly-B pipeline, built on dual variational autoencoders, outperformed every transformer pipeline, including an autoregressive Perceiver model (Omic Translator) and a support-free reformulation of Cisformer, on per-gene and within-cell Spearman correlation in all sixty paired fold comparisons, with 3.8 times shorter training. Transformer pipelines come within 0.02-0.04 on within-cell profile shape but lag by 0.10-0.24 on per-gene correlation. On two withheld cell types per-gene correlation is low; controls show the podocyte values are typical of within-type correlation for seen cell types of the same size, whereas Paneth values match a cell-agnostic shuffle for every Omic Translator arm. Within the transformer family, prespecified ablations show the Perceiver encoder was worth +0.0439 in within-donor per-gene correlation over full self-attention, a chromosome-aware genomic attention prior reduced it by 0.0096 (exact donor-level sign-flip test, Holm-adjusted p = 1.2e-4), and decoder output order had no detectable effect. A training-mean profile reaches 0.314 within-cell correlation with no input and a constant at the true expressed-gene positions reaches 0.996 per-gene correlation, so oracle-support protocols are reported only as diagnostics. Code, results and an audited release are provided.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Predicting RNA abundance from chromatin accessibility lacks fair benchmarks. The authors build a large single-nucleus benchmark and compare seven pipelines, finding a dual-VAE pipeline outperforms transformer models on per-gene prediction, informing virtual-cell expression models.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 从染色质可及性预测RNA丰度缺乏统一基准，不同模型难以公平比较。本文构建覆盖19项研究、126604个单核图谱的基准，在统一峰和基因词表及交叉验证下比较七种流程与两种参考预测器。结果显示基于双变分自编码器的scButterfly-B在逐基因预测上优于多种Transformer流程。该工作为单细胞基因表达预测和虚拟细胞模型提供了可复用的评测框架与基线。

quick_skim.title: Active Learning of Conditional Generative Models via the Transport Neural Tangent Kernel
quick_skim.abstract: Many high-throughput scientific experiments produce distributional outputs, requiring conditional generative models to interpret the data, and to predict outcomes at new inputs. Acquiring experimental data at new conditions (e.g., for a new antigen or a new cell type) is often expensive, motivating the need for automated experimental design methods. However, existing active learning frameworks are limited as they assume scalar or vector-valued outputs. We first show that the Wasserstein test risk of a conditional generative task decomposes into a mean term and a shape term, demonstrating why mean-based active learning is blind to distributional shape. To capture both, we propose the transport Neural Tangent Kernel (tNTK), a tractable kernel that measures how sensitive a generative model's predicted distribution is with respect to its parameters. The tNTK recovers the standard NTK in the deterministic limit and upper-bounds the posterior Fréchet variance of the prediction under small parameter perturbations. It admits a closed-form expression for affine Gaussian transport and tractable Monte Carlo estimators otherwise. Treating the tNTK as the covariance function of a Gaussian process, we greedily select inputs that minimize the total GP posterior variance across the pool, yielding a distribution-aware active learning strategy. We evaluate this strategy across four classes of conditional generative models, including conditional flow matching and conditional Monge gap, on synthetic distributions, intent-labeled sentences, and single-cell perturbation responses. In these experiments, the tNTK outperforms the baseline NTK computed from the conditional mean, demonstrating the value of distribution-aware active learning for generative-modeling tasks.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Active learning for conditional generative models is limited to scalar outputs; the authors propose a transport neural tangent kernel that captures both mean and shape of predicted distributions, enabling efficient design of experiments that predict outcomes at new cell types.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 高维科学实验常产生分布型输出，在新条件（如新细胞类型）采集数据成本高昂，而现有主动学习框架只支持标量或向量输出。作者将条件生成任务的Wasserstein检验风险分解为均值项与形状项，并提出传输神经正切核tNTK以同时捕捉二者。基于该核的主动学习能有效选择实验条件，提升分布型预测效率。这为细胞响应等分布型预测的实验设计提供了可迁移方法。
